study_identification_part.si4_title: Individual deviations from normative models of brain structure in a large cross-sectional schizophrenia cohort

Z-scores were computed to quantify deviation from the 5th and 95th percentiles, with standard deviations derived from bootstrapped confidence intervals. Specific thresholds were defined: z5 < -1.96 for infra-normal and z95 > 1.96 for supra-normal. The AAI was computed as the average of the numerical encoding (+1, 0, -1) across all regions and tracts.

Supra-normal was operationalized as any individual who exceeded the 95% confidence interval for the 95th percentile (i.e., z95 > 1.96), and infra-normal was operationalized as any individual who was below the 5% confidence interval for the 5th percentile (i.e., z5 < -1.96)... clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group differences tested using two-sample t-tests with permutation testing, controlling for age and sex; FDR correction at 5% across regions/tracts using Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. Associations between AAI and polygenic risk score (PRS) tested using Pearson correlation. Canonical correlation analysis (CCA) used to identify multivariate associations between deviation scores (all 116 tracts/regions) and: (1) PRS, and (2) four latent dimensions from ICA (cognitive performance, hallucinations, depressive symptoms, negative symptoms); CCA significance assessed with 5000 permutations controlling familywise error rate. For individual DIP items: two-sample t-tests comparing individuals with infra-normal deviations vs. others, with permutation testing (5000 permutations) and FDR correction at 5% across all regions and DIP items. Supplementary analyses included: correlations between AAI and head motion estimates, correlations between AAI and IQ, correlations between gray matter and white matter AAI, and cross-validation to assess normative range validity.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: While group-level analyses showed widespread reductions in FA and CT in schizophrenia affecting 83% of tracts and 88% of regions, no more than 15-20% of individual patients deviated from normative ranges for any single tract or region, demonstrating marked heterogeneity in anatomical loci of deviations across individuals that is not captured by group-average maps.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Group-level analyses revealed widespread reductions in FA (40 of 48 tracts, 83%) and CT (60 of 68 regions, 88%) in schizophrenia compared to healthy controls (FDR<5%). However, normative modeling revealed profound individual heterogeneity: no more than 17% of patients deviated from normative ranges for any single white matter tract, and no more than 18% for any single cortical region. Despite this, 79% of patients showed infra-normal deviations for at least one locus (vs. 59±2% of healthy individuals, p<0.001), while 46% showed supra-normal deviations for at least one locus (vs. 61±3% of healthy individuals, p<0.001). Infra-normal CT deviations were most common in temporal and ventromedial prefrontal cortices (10-15% of patients), while infra-normal FA deviations were relatively diffuse. Higher polygenic risk for schizophrenia correlated with greater numbers of regions with infra-normal CT deviations (r=-0.17, p=0.006), with temporal regions showing strongest associations in CCA (r=0.69, p=0.044). CCA also identified a marginally significant association between deviation scores and four clinical dimensions (r=0.75, p=0.048). Individual variation in PRS was not significantly correlated with raw measurements of FA and CT. Cross-validation confirmed >90% of healthy individuals resided within the normative range for all regions/tracts. Deviation maps showed significant reproducibility between most site pairs for CT, but lower reproducibility for FA involving Perth and Newcastle sites (smallest cohorts). The correlation between gray matter and white matter AAI was significant (r=0.26, p<0.001), suggesting linked pathology. Current IQ correlated with CT AAI (r=0.16, p=0.008) but not FA AAI.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Individual MRI measurements susceptible to noise and artifacts potentially causing spurious deviations; harmonization of FA data did not fully address inter-site differences for smallest sites (Newcastle, Perth); normative ranges (5-95% percentiles) defined subjectively without clinical validation; potential contributions of medication status, age of onset, and illness duration to heterogeneity not fully addressed; diffusion data acquired on 1.5T scanners with single-shell sequence limiting microstructural specificity; larger normative sample needed to refine percentile confidence intervals; alternative normative modeling techniques not explored
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: First, MRI data are inherently noisy and individual measurements are particularly susceptible to the effects of noise and imaging artifacts. Some individual deviations could have been spurious and owing to noise... Second, while data harmonization was performed to minimize inter-site differences in FA, deviation maps were not reproduced for the two smallest sites (Newcastle, Perth)... Third, normative ranges were operationalized subjectively (5-95% percentiles) and further work is required to determine the minimum thresholds for a deviation to have a clinically meaningful impact. Increasing the size of the normative sample would also assist with refining the normative ranges and their confidence intervals... Fourth, individual variation in medication status, age of onset, and illness duration could potentially contribute to heterogeneity. Fifth, while quantile regression is robust, computationally efficient, statistically unbiased, requires minimal assumptions about the data and enables straightforward evaluation of model fit, alternative normative modeling techniques, moving averages and machine learning should be considered in the future... Finally, the diffusion-weighted MRI data were acquired on 1.5 Tesla scanners using a single-shell acquisition sequence, potentially limiting the ability to investigate more specific microstructural properties other than those from conventional anisotropy measures.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study developed a neural fingerprint approach encoding individual deviation patterns across all tracts and regions as vectors of +1 (supra-normal), 0 (normal), or -1 (infra-normal) for each locus. Independent Component Analysis was used to reduce 82 clinical assessment items into 4 latent dimensions (cognitive performance, hallucinations, depressive symptoms, negative symptoms) for multivariate association analyses. Canonical correlation analysis was employed to identify which specific brain regions contributed most to associations with polygenic risk and clinical dimensions. The Average Abnormality Index (AAI) provided a single whole-brain summary of deviation extent and direction. Reproducibility was assessed by comparing deviation maps independently computed for each of the 5 acquisition sites. Supplementary analyses explored deviations using a higher-resolution Destrieux atlas (148 regions) to establish robustness. The study also examined whether deviations associated with individual DIP symptom items, finding associations between specific symptoms and regional CT deviations after FDR correction.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This study represents one of the early applications of normative modeling to both white matter (FA) and gray matter (CT) in schizophrenia, extending prior work by Wolfers et al. (2018) on GMV. The traveling subject and phantom calibration approach, combined with retrospective harmonization for diffusion MRI, represents a comprehensive multi-level strategy to address scanner differences. The study uses a within-cohort multi-site design (5 sites, all with same Siemens Avanto 1.5T scanners and identical acquisition protocols) which differs from typical multi-site consortia studies. Age of symptom onset was 23.1±6.4 years and duration of illness was 15.8±10.0 years for the schizophrenia group (from Supplementary Table 1). The paper notes that previous analyses in a subset of this cohort found extracellular free water was not significantly elevated in schizophrenia, justifying focus on conventional FA rather than free-water corrected measures. The ASRB exclusion criteria included: any neurological disorder, brain trauma with >24h amnesia, intellectual disability (IQ<70), current drug/alcohol dependence, and ECT in past 6 months. For genotyping: 112 of 128 genome-wide significant SNPs were used for PRS calculation (16 excluded due to >20% missing data or failed imputation QC). The study found that 79% of patients showed infra-normal deviations for at least one locus, suggesting that while deviations are common, their anatomical distribution is highly variable across individuals. CT deviation patterns were more reproducible across sites than FA patterns.
